docs.summary: What a target can actually do.
docs.remarks:
[`TextureFormats`](#api~Prowl.Editor.Build.TextureFormats) is the part the build reads today: it is what [`SelectProcessor`](#api~Prowl.Editor.Build.AssetVariantResolver~SelectProcessor) matches a processor against, so it decides which form of an asset ships. The rest is declared and not yet consumed. [`GraphicsApis`](#api~Prowl.Editor.Build.GraphicsApis) is for choosing shader permutations, which waits on a shader stage, and [`Flags`](#api~Prowl.Editor.Build.TargetCapabilities~Flags) is for failing validation on the desktop before failing on the device.

Everything is a registered string rather than an enum so a platform shipped out of tree can declare a format or a capability this engine has never heard of.
